**GOOGLE AI OVERVIEW:**
An anonymous 14th-century writer known as the Gawain Poet or Pearl Poet wrote Pearl and its companion poems. [Duquesne University +1]
The Pearl Manuscript Collection — All four core works survive in a single 14th-century vellum manuscript (Cotton Nero A.x): [Poetry Foundation +1] Pearl: A dream vision where a grieving father talks to a heavenly maiden representing his lost toddler. Sir Gawain and the Green Knight: An Arthurian chivalric romance. Cleanness (or Purity): Biblical narrative poems on moral themes. Patience: A poetic paraphrase of the biblical book of Jonah. [Wikipedia +5]
Note: Some scholars also suggest the same author wrote Saint Erkenwald, though it is not in the same manuscript. [Miami Dade College +1]
Explore More — Read the Middle English texts or translations via the Middle English Texts Series. Check historical context and manuscript details on the Poetry Foundation Gawain Poet Profile.
Suggested Follow-Ups — Want to read a modern translation? J.R.R. Tolkien translated Pearl alongside Sir Gawain and the Green Knight. Curious about the language? These works use a late-medieval North-West Midlands dialect distinct from Geoffrey Chaucer's London English.
